card.title: Stay for the Hard Part
card.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wasn't just late to the reunion. Can I tell you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I waited outside for half an hour. Can you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd be happier without me there. Will you sit beside me now?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 hints at more than lateness, A3 admits waiting outside and A5 reveals fear of being unwanted while asking for the offered seat now.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 traffic assumption causes A3 correction; B4 belief A avoided B causes A5 the contrary desire and underlying fear.

relationship.evidence: B2 saved a seat and B4 remains present while honestly naming their own hurt interpretation.

heightening.evidence: B4 reassurance plus vulnerability elicits A5 a deeper confession and a renewed concrete request for togetherness.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion and B2 saved seat establish the missed connection and who offered it.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 wanted that seat keeps the emotional reveal attached to the concrete gesture; wit stays 3.
